title: How Buffett picks people, stays in his circle of competence, and ignores the crowd
summary: At UGA's Terry College, Buffett explains how to choose a career, why character beats grades, how to value any business as discounted future cash, and why staying inside your circle of competence matters. He also covers his own mistakes (Berkshire, US Air, omissions), why temperament beats IQ, and why small businesses can beat giants.

principles.text: Work for someone you admire, not whatever looks best on your resume.
principles.quote: go to work for whomever you admire the most and I said you can't get a bad result you'll jump out of bed in the morning and you'll be having fun

principles.text: Hire for intelligence, energy and integrity; without integrity, you want them lazy and dumb.
principles.quote: we look for three things when we hire people we look for intelligence we look for for initiative or energy and we look for integrity and if they don't have the ladder the first two will kill you

principles.text: Intrinsic value is all the cash a business will give you from now to Judgment Day, discounted properly.
principles.quote: all the cash that a b a business would give you between now and Judgment Day discounted at the proper discount rate that number is what the intrinsic value of business is

principles.text: Define your circle of competence and stay inside it; its size matters less than knowing its edge.
principles.quote: defining your circle of competence is the most important aspect of investing it's not how important how how large your circle is you don't have to be an expert on everything but knowing where the perimeter of that Circle

principles.text: Prefer a wonderful business at a fair price to a fair business at a wonderful price; time rewards great businesses and punishes lousy ones.
principles.quote: I rather buy a wonderful business at a fair price than a fair business at a wonderful price

principles.text: His biggest mistakes are omissions: clear opportunities within his competence that he failed to seize.
principles.quote: the biggest mistakes I've made by far are mistakes of omission and not Co Mission I mean it's the things I knew enough to do they were within my circle of competence and I was sucking my thumb
